title: Generic residue extensions and finite generic fibres
statement: Let $S$ be a Noetherian scheme, meaning it admits a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and let $f:X\to S$ be of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Assume every generic point of an irreducible component of $X$ maps to a generic point of a component of $S$ [def-weil-irreducible-components, def-sc-generic-point]. Then the following are equivalent: (i) for each such generic point $x$, $\kappa(x)/\kappa(f(x))$ is a finite field extension [def-weil-residue-field, def-pc-field-extension]; (ii) there is a dense open $V\subseteq S$ such that $f^{-1}(V)\to V$ is finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Under either condition, for every generic point $s$ of $S$ the scheme fibre $X_s=X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ is finite over $\kappa(s)$ [def-pc-fibre-product, def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-pc-scheme-fibre].

source.place: Expose II Proposition 1.1.7, printed p. 24; the finite generic-fibre consequence is restriction of the finite map in (ii).

proof.text: Finite type includes local finite type and quasi-compactness. Since $S$ is Noetherian, $X$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. Its irreducible components are finite in number by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finitely-many-components], and each has a unique generic point by [lem-sc-scheme-sober]. Also $X$ is quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated], and hence $f$ is quasi-separated by clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence]. These conclusions hold without separatedness or reducedness assumptions on $f,X,S$.

source.place: Tags 01T6 (lemma-finite-type-noetherian) and 01T7 (lemma-finite-type-Noetherian-quasi-separated); properties.tex Tags 0BA8 and 01OY; schemes.tex Tag 01KV

proof.text: Assume (i), fix a component generic point $s$ of $S$, and take $x\in f^{-1}(s)$. By [lem-sc-irreducible-components-cover] choose an irreducible component $C$ of $X$ containing $x$, and by [lem-sc-scheme-sober] let $\xi$ be its generic point. Thus $x\in\overline{\{\xi\}}$. Continuity gives $s\in\overline{\{f(\xi)\}}$. Maximal dominance says $f(\xi)$ is a component generic point. The inclusion of the component $\overline{\{s\}}$ into the component $\overline{\{f(\xi)\}}$ must be equality by maximality; uniqueness of generic points then gives $f(\xi)=s$. By (i), $\kappa(\xi)/\kappa(s)$ is finite, so [lem-trf-finite-residue-point-closed-in-fibre] makes $\xi$ closed in $X_s$. Under the subspace identification in [def-pc-scheme-fibre], $x$ is still a specialization of $\xi$, so $x=\xi$. Consequently $f^{-1}(s)$ is a subset of the finite set of component generic points of $X$ obtained in Step 1, and is finite (possibly empty).

source.place: Tag 01TE (lemma-algebraic-residue-field-extension-closed-point-fibre); schemes.tex Tags 01IS and 01K1; topology.tex Tag 004W; elaboration of ILO II Proposition 1.1.7, (ii) implies (i)

proof.text: Step 2 proves finite set-theoretic fibres over every component generic point of $S$. Step 1 gives quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness of $f$, and local finite type, while $S$ is Noetherian by hypothesis. These are exactly the hypotheses of [lem-weil-pbc-generic-finite-morphism-open-neighborhood]. It supplies a dense open $V\subseteq S$ containing every component generic point and with $f^{-1}(V)\to V$ finite. This proves (i) implies (ii).

source.place: Tag 02NW, lemma-generically-finite, (1) equivalent to (4), at all component generic points

proof.text: Now assume (ii). Every component generic point $s$ of $S$ belongs to $V$. Indeed, there are finitely many irreducible components of $S$ by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finitely-many-components]. If $C=\overline{\{s\}}$, let $W$ be the complement of the union of the other components. Their closedness and maximality imply $W$ is open, contains $s$, and is contained in $C$. Density gives $v\in W\cap V$. Since $v\in\overline{\{s\}}$, the open neighbourhood $V$ of $v$ contains $s$. The component and generic-point conventions are [def-weil-irreducible-components, def-sc-generic-point].

For any such $s\in V$, the fibre $X_s\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ is the base change of the finite restriction $f^{-1}(V)\to V$ along $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)\to V$. The universal property of the fibre product identifies this base change with the fibre of $f$; the point morphism factors through $V$ because its image is $s$. By clause (a) of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence], $X_s$ is finite over $\kappa(s)$. This proves the final assertion under (ii), and under (i) by Step 3. Here [def-pc-scheme-fibre] specifies the fibre and its structure map.

Let $x$ be a component generic point of $X$ and put $s=f(x)$, a component generic point by maximal dominance. By Steps 4 and 5, $X_s$ is finite over $k=\kappa(s)$. By [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] it is $\operatorname{Spec}B$ for a finite-dimensional $k$-algebra $B$. The point induced by $x$ corresponds to a prime $\mathfrak q$ of $B$. The quotient $B/\mathfrak q$ is a finite-dimensional domain, hence a field by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-dimensional-domain-is-field]. It is therefore its own fraction field, so the residue field of this fibre point is $B/\mathfrak q$, finite over $k$. Finally [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-point-residue-field] identifies that residue field with $\kappa(x)$ as an extension of $k$: its tensor product is $\kappa(x)\otimes_k k\cong\kappa(x)$, whose sole prime is zero. Thus $\kappa(x)/\kappa(f(x))$ is finite, proving (ii) implies (i).
